rows.gapCause: BASELINE ISOLATION ROUND (doors `capture.control-baseline-mint` + `fuse.control-element-delta`) — re-recorded DELIBERATELY. The control the styled-channel door subtracts was mounted INSIDE `mount.wrapperOpen`, in the SAME document as the component, so every page-global rule the library ships styled the CONTROL too and was then cancelled as if it were a user-agent default: shadcn's `* { border-color: var(--border) }`, the tailwind/astryx/shadcn preflight family (`border-style: solid`, `border-width: 0`, `box-sizing: border-box`, `tab-size`, `text-size-adjust`, `appearance`, `cursor`), and the polaris/fluent/carbon/altitude provider ink + body font-family + line-height. That is the invisible shadcn Input (1px border, no colour) and the inkless polaris/fluent text. The baseline is now measured on a page carrying the browser, the colour-scheme and the stage box and NOTHING the library ships (`capture.captureUaControls`, backfilled into every committed capture by `extract/computed/ua-baseline-backfill.ts`); custom properties (`--*`) keep the in-page baseline by name, because a `:root` token block inherits onto every part and is refused downstream anyway. MEASURED across all 116 committed captures, offline re-fuse: +4,783 (part,channel) cells newly carried, 365 dropped — and every one of the 365 proved EQUAL to the user-agent default, i.e. it had been carried only because the POLLUTED control disagreed with the browser. antd moves by ZERO cells (cssinjs, scoped class names, no page-global rule at all), which is the no-noise half of the measurement. PINNED-BROWSER ROUND (v1-integration-2 2026-08-25) — re-recorded DELIBERATELY under the browser the capture was taken on. The receipt could not say so: `regate.ts` sets `browserVersion` from the CAPTURE's `_provenance.browser`, so every regate.scorecard.json printed the capture's browser no matter which binary actually rendered the gate page. MEASURED DIRECTLY on both binaries. On bare default-styled elements (9 tags, full computed-style property set) exactly ONE property differs: `position-anchor`, `none` in 149 and `normal` in 151. On a RAW replay over EVERY enumerated channel (the committed polaris Button, 4,142,880 cells) FOUR differ: `flex-line-count`, `position-anchor`, `ruby-overhang`, `text-fit` — precisely the set that `evals/fixtures/computed-floor-platform-baseline.json` ALREADY excludes on linux and calls platform-sensitivity. Across THIS baseline's 116 rows, where the styled-channel door has been applied, `position-anchor` is the ONLY one of the four appearing in any recorded mismatch list (the other three: zero scorecards). `cellsCompared` does not shift by ONE cell on ANY of the 116 rows (918,995 before and after) while corpus `cellsEqual` rises 766,991 -> 773,204. The corpus splits along the CAPTURE browser: 79 of the 116 committed captures were themselves taken on 151, where base and UA control agree so `fuse.control-element-delta` SUBTRACTS position-anchor and it is never carried — those rows do not move at all; the other 37 were taken on 149 with the UA control backfilled on 151, so position-anchor DISAGREES with the control, is carried, and was then scored against a 151 render. This re-record ran with PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_PATH=chromium-1228 and reproduces CI run 32867181394 EXACTLY on all 51 rows CI had an opinion about (37 moved + 14 refusals). No engine change is involved: the consolidated engine (#43–#48, including #45's pure-UA control baseline) is the SAME engine the previous baseline was recorded on. THIS ROW ROSE: offline 86.179 -> 89.431 on an UNCHANGED denominator of 984 cells — 32 position-anchor cells that had been scored against a 151 render are EQUAL when rendered on the capture's OWN pinned browser. This capture is one of the 37 taken on Chromium 149. Nothing was widened, excused or excluded: the same cells are compared and more of them agree.
